title: A Mistake Has Been Made
author: John Packer
paragraphs: Our city is less than a year old and many good people have volunteered countless hours in getting our city on its feet. Our mayor and city council are at the top of that list of people we should all be grateful for and go out of our way to express our appreciation. As they move forward, on our behalf, they will inevitably make a few mistakes. How they respond to those mistakes is critical to the success of our city.

Before reading Gordon Auchhinclass’s recent Guest Commentary: In His Own Hand: The History Behind Our City’s Name, I knew a few troubling facts about Peter Odgen. I knew he was not an American, but a British foreign agent sent here to stop any American settlement of this valley. I did not know he was a murderer and intended to use the extermination of Indians and beavers to accomplish his purpose. He was the first white man to come here, but naming our city after such a foul individual is a big mistake. The term “Whitewashing” seems to apply here.

The second part of this mistake is going against the will of the majority of the residents. A survey was conducted and the clear result was NOT to use the name Ogden. We voted to form this city because the county was overriding our desires and we wanted our voice heard. How ironic that in the first major decision of our newly elected representees, the voice of the residents was once more overridden.

There are two ways to respond when we realize we have made a mistake: Change the mistake or dig in our heals. I hope that our newly elected representatives, who have made many good decisions and donated countless hours on our behalf, will do the right thing. Will they respond to this mistake with humility or hubris?

John Packer,
Huntsville

title: An Inconvenient Set of Facts Mr. O’ Neglected to Mention
author: Lonnie D. Crockett, Ph.D.
paragraphs: Re: “What if Trump Declares a National Emergency to Nullify the 2026 Elections?”

Mr. O’s final pre-election letter calls the right to vote “the essence of American Democracy.” A fine sentiment, but our Founders deliberately gave us a Republic, not a Democracy. Article IV, Section 4 guarantees every state “a Republican Form of Government,” and we pledge allegiance “to [that] Republic for which it stands.” James Madison, in Federalist No. 10, warned that Democracies “have ever been spectacles of turbulence and contention,” and “as short in their lives as they are violent in their deaths.” A Republic restrains majorities and presidents alike with a written Constitution and defends the minority from the majority.  A Democracy is simply 3 wolves and 2 Sheep voting on what to have for supper.

That Constitution answers Mr. O’s central fear. His headline is a “what if,” and by his own wording Trump only “may” declare an emergency. Article I, Section 4 leaves the “Times, Places and Manner” of elections to the States and Congress, not the President. No emergency declaration can cancel an election, and Mr. O’ concedes it when he names the real defenders of the vote: State Officials, the courts and the voters.

Mr. O’ calls election-integrity measures “voter suppression” but sets no supportable facts that show voters are or have been suppressed.  Voter ID, Citizenship verification and clean rolls are ordinary and wise safeguards, and polling has long shown majorities of both party’s favor photo ID and proof of Citizenship.

He insists there is “no credible proof of voter fraud.” Fraud is hard to prove because it is meant to be hidden, but it is not imaginary. People have been prosecuted for tampering with ballots and voting illegally in several states. Here in Utah, eleven people were charged in 2025 with forgery and fraud in signature gathering for Cox to qualify as a candidate after he was soundly out voted by the Convention Delegates for our 2024 primary ballot. Confidence in elections is earned by checking the work.

Then comes the list of grievances. Prices: consumer prices rose roughly 20 percent from 2021 to 2025, before Trump’s term began, and no one can honestly blame the Trump administration. Immigration: ICE is no “vigilante force.” Both parties of Congress created it to enforce immigration laws that Congress wrote and was approved by both parties, and federal judges reviewed its actions; Mr. O’ Calling its detention system “gulags” is rhetoric, not argument. Allies and wars: demanding that allies carry their fair share of their own defense is a policy choice, not betrayal, and war powers remain checked by Congress and the voters. Executive orders: when a court finds an order unlawful, it is enjoined, which proves our system of checks and balances works. Approval ratings and “broken promises” are for the voters to judge in November.
Citizens who love our Republic should vote, insist on honest and verifiable elections, and hold every officeholder, of both parties, to the Constitution.
Lonnie D. Crockett, Ph.D.

title: Hearing Versus Listening
author: John Anderson
paragraphs: On the front page of the November 1, 2026, issue of the “Ogden Valley News” newspaper our City Council asked for feedback on the revised city seal. This, in the wake of naming our new city. What evidence do we have that our input will make a difference? You will have to make up your own mind, but here are a few things to consider.

The “Mayor’s Message” published in the same newspaper with the same issue date was well written and characterized much of how I and you likely feel. Political leaders practice saying what we like to hear. Sometimes what they say is genuine. I believe our mayor is sincere. I will say here that I am grateful to her and our City Council for their willingness to serve our community. It is a tremendous responsibility and consequently not many are willing to step up and be held accountable for it. Continuing however, the message was a bit contradictory and highlighted the failure of our city’s first political litmus test. Need I rehash the details? It had to do with naming our new city.

The mayor’s article encouraged us to “Show up and be heard.” She went on to say that one of her “personal guiding principles” is, “Decisions are made by those who show up.” For the most part, precisely. This should apply to those who doubted the veracity of the name surveys (plural). They claimed, in essence, that the surveys were skewed because of a lack of opposing “votes”. In other words, if others had taken the survey, the outcome might possibly have favored the name Ogden and not Eden.  Three formal, published surveys later, and none favored the name Ogden---by a long shot.  If the Ogden Ites wished to prevail in the survey, they should have shown up to vote. Well, we all know what happened. In the end, the surveys did not matter. All the time and resources that went in to them sadly had no effect on the ultimate outcome. May I apologize on behalf of someone, to those good people who sacrificed their time, energies, and other resources to provide a service that was ignored in the end. Where is the incentive to ever conduct a city survey again? I will talk about trust later.

Back to the Mayor’s article. The heading to her message says, “Your voice. Your Valley. Your future.” It speaks of ‘our shared responsibility to decide what kind of community we want to become.’ Our shared responsibilities cannot be shared if our leaders refuse to listen. The article’s first bullet point says, “Listening First”. Good point. If minds are made up beforehand though, then listening becomes a mere exercise in hearing, and there is no “representation”.
The second bullet point says, “Community discussion”. Again, if no one is really listening, then there is no incentive for dialogue.

The third bullet point says, “Now it’s your turn”. It mentions the ‘collective vision of our community and not the opinions of a “select few”.’ The City’s new-name surveys were “the community”. The “select few” was the City Council.

Let’s return to “Show up and be heard”, the final bullet point in the mayor’s article. Those who took the initiative to complete the name surveys “showed up”, but the democratic process was overruled and politics prevailed.

Now, as it usually goes, well as it did go, reasons are given for why we should just move on, such as, “We have bigger fish to fry” or “Let’s stop beating a dead horse (my apologies)”, and etc. Like the way we might distract our kids from an important (to them) fixation that we preemptively and unilaterally overrule. We might expect our city fathers (and mothers) to say something like, “We will try and do better next time”. Fine. However, that does not change the fact that we still have a city name that the preponderance of opinions rejected. Before going forward, we can and must revisit naming our city…and give it a name chosen by the people and not the “select few”. I have more to say and hope to be given the chance to return and share some thoughts about TRUST and the name, Ogden. Until next time.

John Anderson, 
Eden

title: A Quiet Valley Is a Shared Responsibility
author: James Diefenderfer
paragraphs: Anyone who lives in the Ogden Valley knows why we're here: open sky, mountain air, and the kind of quiet you can actually hear. With so much development underway, that quiet is getting harder to come by, which makes it all the more precious when we have it. As more neighbors discover what we love about this place, it's worth reminding ourselves how to protect it.

Dogs are part of valley life, and most people wouldn't have it any other way. A dog that barks four or five times at a passing deer, a delivery truck, or a coyote at dusk is simply being a dog. Five to ten barks usually means something is off. The dog may be bored, anxious, hot, cold, or in need of attention. Beyond that, when barking goes on and on, it is rarely the dog's problem. It's an owner who hasn't noticed or hasn't acted.

The rules are already on the books. Ogden Valley City, which includes Eden, has not adopted its own animal code, so the Weber County Code applies. Sec. 6-4-13(6), Nuisance Animals, deems an animal a nuisance if it "makes unreasonable barking, whining, howling, or disturbing noises." Huntsville has its own rules. Town Code Title 12, Section 12.15, Loud or Offensive Animals, states that no one may "own, keep, or harbor any dog which by loud, continued, or frequent barking, howling, yelping, or by noxious or offensive odors, or in any other manner, shall annoy, disturb, or endanger the health and welfare of any person or neighborhood." These rules aren't meant to punish anyone. They reflect a basic expectation that we consider the people living next to us.

If you're a dog owner, a few habits go a long way. Bring your dog inside at night. Make sure it has exercise, company, and shade or shelter. Check in on what's happening when you're away. If your dog is a barker, a trainer or your vet can help.
If you're bothered by a neighbor's dog, start with a friendly conversation. Most people simply don't know, and a kind word solves far more than a complaint ever will.
Our valley is growing, but the character of our community is ours to keep. A little awareness and a little courtesy will protect the peace that brought us all here.

James Diefenderfer,
Eden

title: What if Trump Declares a National Emergency to Nullify the 2026 Elections?
author: James M. O’Brien
paragraphs: This is my final letter to the editor before the midterm elections. Although you may disagree with my political opinions, I hope we can agree that our right to vote is the essence of American democracy. Donald Trump’s twin assaults on this right—first falsely asserting voter fraud and then pushing voter-suppression measures in the guise of election integrity protection—are the subjects of this letter.

The November elections are a de facto referendum on Trump’s second-term. Trump has broken critical 2024 campaign promises (e.g., righting the economy, avoiding foreign wars, deporting the “worst of the worst”). He has shown himself incapable of governing except by often-illegal executive orders. He has increased the cost of living by thousands of dollars per family with no benefit for them in return. He has shown himself unfit to be commander-in-chief. Trump has undermined our allies and been manipulated by our adversaries. Trump has built a vigilante ICE force and a network of deportation gulags. He has violated the Constitution, U.S. law and international law.

With all-time-low approval ratings, Trump now faces the reality of losing control of Congress. Trump cannot stomach losing. After Joe Biden’s 2020 victory, Trump hollered “crooked” and orchestrated the unsuccessful January 6th coup. Trump now may declare a national emergency based on unproven election fraud and try to nullify the 2026 election results. If judicially sustained, such Executive action would mean the end to 250 years of American democracy. Nullification would be both unlawful and disgraceful, but an act befitting a president who tastelessly staged an MMA boxing match at the White House as part of America’s Semiquincentennial celebrations.

Although the courts normally defer to a president’s national emergency determinations, Trump’s cries of election fraud should not be entitled to this “presumption of regularity.” MAGA pundits began urging this national emergency gambit upon Trump months ago solely as a means of retaining political power despite the expected loss of the popular vote in 2026. Trump has asserted 2020 election fraud in over 60 lawsuits, all of which the courts have rejected. The Trump DoJ’s and FBI’s renewed investigations since 2025, still have uncovered no credible proof of voter fraud. Nevertheless, the president periodically asserts large illegal voter numbers in specific states which upon further research prove illusory and based on incomplete/inaccurate data. The emergency always has been a concocted stratagem, never a real threat to the nation!

What then stands between Trump and a second coup?  Last-line defenders are the States’ election officials, voting-rights organizations, the courts and American voters. The States and voting-rights organizations have been gameplaying various election interference scenarios and preparing for litigation to rapidly challenge Trump’s interference (whatever form it takes). The courts will continue to follow the facts and law in deciding these disputes. Finally, American voters (like you and me) must turn out en mass to vote and, if necessary, protest resolutely against presidential interference.  If we love our democracy, we all must defend the right to vote.

title: Thank You for Supporting Us!
author: Boni and Glenn Croydon
paragraphs: It’s a wrap! Ogden Valley Farm hosted its first stand on May 2, and now twenty-two Saturdays later, we have ended our first season, providing baked goods, organically grown produce and flowers, fresh eggs, two hours of free live, local music, and, most importantly, a “gathering place” for residents of and visitors to the valley. The opening day included the music of “Hit N Miss,” which inspired the idea of providing music every Saturday throughout the season.

Rain or sun, the corner of Highway 39 and 6525 E, across from the west end of Anderson Cove Campgrounds and adjacent to St. Florence Catholic Church, became a bustling location for discovering garlic and rosemary focaccia bread, British-style scones, both cranberry orange and blueberry lemon cream cheese, and Amish Farm Stand Cinnamon rolls backed by Glenn, who proudly wears the t-shirt, “I bake bread and I know things.” Boni added Morning Glory Muffins and Banana Blueberry Muffins, Lavender Shortbread Cookies, Bon Appetit Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies with Sea Salt, “Opala”/Garbage Cookies from Hawaii with macadamia nuts, Energy Bars, and Gluten-free Almond Flour Crackers!

When the lavender on the farm was harvested, lavender bouquets were joined by other popular lavender products including hand painted sachets, bath salts, sugar, and syrup.
Flower bouquets were offered with freshly picked snapdragons, zinnias, cosmos, calendula, and basil sprigs and lavender tucked in.

Produce became more available as the weeks passed with tomatoes from the gigantic plants in the greenhouse, picked when requested lettuce mixes, with choices made by the visitors as to what greens they wanted included, including edible flowers. Kale, chard, yellow globe tomatoes, and New Zealand spinach were soon offered in season. Glenn loved having a chance to share his knowledge and love of the garden with those who were touring the gardens and discovering what they could serve to family and guests. Eventually, green beans, zucchini, and yellow squash began to contribute to what was being offered.
Famer Dale from Hooper blessed all of us with his delivery of fresh corn, cucumbers, onions, bell peppers, and other peppers, “guaranteed” red crimson watermelon with seeds, and cantaloupe. Jessica of Dandelion Farms helped us try to meet the demands of folks seeking fresh, free-range eggs, while we were waiting (trying to do so patiently) for some of our chickens to reach the egg-laying stage of their lives. 
Many of you had the chance to meet Alan, who comes out four days a week to help us maintain the garden and the chicken coops, set up the farm stand, develop the new high tunnel, weed, design and build the decks between the greenhouse and the high tunnel, clean and make improvements. He is an extremely hard-working young man who is capable, willing, and eager to do so much that Boni and Glenn, at 78 and 81, just can’t easily accomplish!
Thank you for supporting us! We still are eager to share what we and our farm produce without having a weekly farmstand. Call Glenn at 385-405-6412 to let us know what we can provide in the way of produce, baked goods, and eggs for you, your family and friends. We have loved this inaugural year, and we look forward to “growing” into the future!

title: Eden Resident Needs Your Help
author: Michael White
paragraphs: Hi Valley residents,
My name is Michael White, a valley resident for over twenty years, and having worked up here since 1979 starting out at Powder Mountain and other hospitality businesses over the years.
I'm calling upon you if you have it in your heart to donate for my quest to get a kidney transplant as I have stage 5 kidney disease and I'm currently on dialysis 3 days a week.
My story starts in 2017 getting into an automobile crash in Ogden Canyon while working for a local landscaping company.

This in itself was very traumatic event which over time not allowing me to walk properly and I believe contributing to my current situation although many years later.
Some of you may know many not but every dollar helps to my cause.
I have a GoFundMe setup in my name for those who wish to contribute at https://gofund.me/749ae9b8e
Thank you
caption: Michael White
